# dlasr

> Applies a sequence of real plane rotations to a real general rectangular matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlasr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlasr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlasr( order, side, pivot, direct, M, N, c, strideC, s, strideS, A, LDA ) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `side` | `OperationSide` | in |  | one of `'left'`, `'right'` | `'left'` or `'right'` |
| `pivot` | `("variable"\|"top"\|"bottom")` | in |  | one of `'bottom'`, `'top'`, `'variable'` | `'variable'`, `'top'`, or `'bottom'` |
| `direct` | `("forward"\|"backward")` | in |  | one of `'backward'`, `'forward'` | `'forward'` or `'backward'` |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `M ≥ 0` | number of rows of A |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns of A |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | in | `( side === 'left' ) ? M - 1 : N - 1` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | in |  |  | `c` stride length |
| `s` | `Float64Array` | in | `( side === 'left' ) ? M - 1 : N - 1` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | in |  |  | `s` stride length |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `M × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, M )`; row-major requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`: Specifies whether the plane rotation matrix P is applied to A on the left or the right.

  -   `= 'L'`: Left, compute A := $P \, A$
  -   `= 'R'`: Right, compute A:= $A \, P^T$
- `pivot`: Specifies the plane for which P(k) is a plane rotation matrix.

  -   `= 'V'`: Variable pivot, the plane (k,k+1)
  -   `= 'T'`: Top pivot, the plane (1,k+1)
  -   `= 'B'`: Bottom pivot, the plane (k,z)
- `direct`: Specifies whether P is a forward or backward sequence of plane rotations.

  -   `= 'F'`: Forward, $P = P(z-1)$\*...\*$P(2) \, P(1)$
  -   `= 'B'`: Backward, $P = P(1) \, P(2)$\*...\*P(z-1)
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. If $m \le 1$, an immediate return is effected.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. If $n \le 1$, an immediate return is effected.
- `c`: (N-1) if `SIDE = 'R'` The cosines c(k) of the plane rotations.
- `s`: (N-1) if `SIDE = 'R'` The sines s(k) of the plane rotations. The 2-by-2 plane rotation part of the matrix P(k), R(k), has the form $R(k) = ( c(k) s(k) )$ ( -s(k) c(k) ).
- `A`: The M-by-N matrix A. On exit, A is overwritten by $P \, A$ if `SIDE = 'L'` or by $A \, P^T$ if `SIDE = 'R'`.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: output array

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid operation side
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "bottom", "top", "variable"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be one of the following: "backward", "forward"
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlasr.ndarray(
    side, pivot, direct,
    M, N,
    c, strideC, offsetC,
    s, strideS, offsetS,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA
) → Float64Array
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `side` | `OperationSide` | in |  | one of `'left'`, `'right'` | `'left'` or `'right'` |
| `pivot` | `("variable"\|"top"\|"bottom")` | in |  | one of `'bottom'`, `'top'`, `'variable'` | `'variable'`, `'top'`, or `'bottom'` |
| `direct` | `("forward"\|"backward")` | in |  | one of `'backward'`, `'forward'` | `'forward'` or `'backward'` |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `M ≥ 0` | number of rows of A |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns of A |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | in | `( side === 'left' ) ? M - 1 : N - 1` |  | array of cosines |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `c` |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `c` |
| `s` | `Float64Array` | in | `( side === 'left' ) ? M - 1 : N - 1` |  | array of sines |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `s` |
| ↳ `offsetS` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `s` |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `M × N` |  | input/output matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for A |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`: Specifies whether the plane rotation matrix P is applied to A on the left or the right.

  -   `= 'L'`: Left, compute A := $P \, A$
  -   `= 'R'`: Right, compute A:= $A \, P^T$
- `pivot`: Specifies the plane for which P(k) is a plane rotation matrix.

  -   `= 'V'`: Variable pivot, the plane (k,k+1)
  -   `= 'T'`: Top pivot, the plane (1,k+1)
  -   `= 'B'`: Bottom pivot, the plane (k,z)
- `direct`: Specifies whether P is a forward or backward sequence of plane rotations.

  -   `= 'F'`: Forward, $P = P(z-1)$\*...\*$P(2) \, P(1)$
  -   `= 'B'`: Backward, $P = P(1) \, P(2)$\*...\*P(z-1)
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. If $m \le 1$, an immediate return is effected.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. If $n \le 1$, an immediate return is effected.
- `c`: (N-1) if `SIDE = 'R'` The cosines c(k) of the plane rotations.
- `s`: (N-1) if `SIDE = 'R'` The sines s(k) of the plane rotations. The 2-by-2 plane rotation part of the matrix P(k), R(k), has the form $R(k) = ( c(k) s(k) )$ ( -s(k) c(k) ).
- `A`: The M-by-N matrix A. On exit, A is overwritten by $P \, A$ if `SIDE = 'L'` or by $A \, P^T$ if `SIDE = 'R'`.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: A

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid operation side
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "bottom", "top", "variable"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "backward", "forward"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlasr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlasr';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );

// Cosines and sines of the N-1 plane rotations ( c[k]^2 + s[k]^2 = 1 ):
const c = new Float64Array( [ 0.6, 0.8 ] );
const s = new Float64Array( [ 0.8, 0.6 ] );

// Using the standard interface (apply P = P(2)*P(1) from the left):
dlasr( 'row-major', 'left', 'variable', 'forward', N, N, c, 1, s, 1, A, N );
console.log( A ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface (apply the same rotations in backward order, P = P(1)*P(2)):
dlasr.ndarray( 'left', 'variable', 'backward', N, N, c, 1, 0, s, 1, 0, A, N, 1, 0 );
console.log( A ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLASR`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLASR applies a sequence of plane rotations to a real matrix A, from either the left or the right.

When `SIDE = 'L'`, the transformation takes the form

$$
A := P \, A
$$

and when `SIDE = 'R'`, the transformation takes the form

$$
A := A \, P^T
$$

where P is an orthogonal matrix consisting of a sequence of z plane rotations, with $z = M$ when `SIDE = 'L'` and $z = N$ when `SIDE = 'R'`, and $P^T$ is the transpose of P.

When `DIRECT = 'F'` (Forward sequence), then

$$
P = P(z-1) \, \cdots \, P(2) \, P(1)
$$

and when `DIRECT = 'B'` (Backward sequence), then

$$
P = P(1) \, P(2) \, \cdots \, P(z-1)
$$

where P(k) is a plane rotation matrix defined by the 2-by-2 rotation

$$
R(k) = ( c(k) s(k) )
$$

$$
= ( -s(k) c(k) )
$$

When `PIVOT = 'V'` (Variable pivot), the rotation is performed for the plane (k,k+1), i.e., P(k) has the form

$$
P(k) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 &  &  &  &  &  &  &  \\  & .. &  &  &  &  &  &  \\  &  & 1 &  &  &  &  &  \\  &  &  & c(k) & s(k) &  &  &  \\  &  &  & -s(k) & c(k) &  &  &  \\  &  &  &  &  & 1 &  &  \\  &  &  &  &  &  & .. &  \\  &  &  &  &  &  &  & 1 \end{pmatrix}
$$

where R(k) appears as a rank-2 modification to the identity matrix in rows and columns k and k+1.

When `PIVOT = 'T'` (Top pivot), the rotation is performed for the plane (1,k+1), so P(k) has the form

$$
P(k) = \begin{pmatrix} c(k) &  &  &  & s(k) &  &  &  \\  & 1 &  &  &  &  &  &  \\  &  & .. &  &  &  &  &  \\  &  &  & 1 &  &  &  &  \\ -s(k) &  &  &  & c(k) &  &  &  \\  &  &  &  &  & 1 &  &  \\  &  &  &  &  &  & .. &  \\  &  &  &  &  &  &  & 1 \end{pmatrix}
$$

where R(k) appears in rows and columns 1 and k+1.

Similarly, when `PIVOT = 'B'` (Bottom pivot), the rotation is performed for the plane (k,z), giving P(k) the form

$$
P(k) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 &  &  &  &  &  &  &  \\  & .. &  &  &  &  &  &  \\  &  & 1 &  &  &  &  &  \\  &  &  & c(k) &  &  &  & s(k) \\  &  &  &  & 1 &  &  &  \\  &  &  &  &  & .. &  &  \\  &  &  &  &  &  & 1 &  \\  &  &  & -s(k) &  &  &  & c(k) \end{pmatrix}
$$

where R(k) appears in rows and columns k and z. The rotations are performed without ever forming P(k) explicitly.

</section>
